title: Hermits on Carmel (c. 1200)

lines: A PROPHET, FACE TO HIS KNEES.
cards: A long green ridge runs down to the sea on the coast of the Holy Land, and at its top a man is crouched on the ground, his face pressed between his knees.

He has just come through a very public day: a crowd, an altar, fire from heaven, the story you met on day four hundred ten. Now he has climbed away to pray alone, while his servant keeps going to look out at the sea.
The man is the prophet Elijah, Elias in the Douay-Rheims, and the ridge is Mount Carmel.

teach.b: Carmelite: someone who belongs to Carmel, to the order that grew up on that mountain. Start with Elijah, because the hermits did.
In the third book of Kings, as the Douay-Rheims names it, Elijah stands on Carmel and calls a wavering people to choose the Lord. Fire falls on his offering.
Then, the text says, he goes up to the top of Carmel, bows to the ground, and "put his face between his knees."
He prays and keeps praying, and his servant keeps going back to watch the sea, until at last a little cloud rises out of the sea, small as a man's foot, and the drought breaks in rain.
That's the picture the hermits treasured. Not the fire. The man alone on the mountaintop, praying low and waiting.
Much later, tradition says, a small group of Western Christians, pilgrims and penitents from Europe, settled on Carmel as hermits.
They lived in caves and small cells on the slope, near a spring that tradition linked to Elijah.
They looked to Elijah as their model, and in time dedicated their life to Mary too; tradition says they built a little chapel in her honor.

teach.h: ELIJAH AND MARY: A DOUBLE INHERITANCE.
teach.b: That double inheritance is still in the order's full name: the Brothers of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary of Mount Carmel.

teach.h: A LITTLE CLOUD, LIKE A MAN'S FOOT.
teach.b: Later the Carmelites would spread far from the mountain, and saints would come from Spain and France and elsewhere. But it begins small: a few people, a ridge, a spring, and a prophet's posture of waiting prayer.

how: Carmelite friars, nuns and lay Carmelites look to Elijah and to Mary as models, and give a central place in their lives to silent, personal prayer.

games.q: you're Elijah. the fire has fallen, the crowd has seen it, the day is yours. what do you do next?
o: stay with the crowd and celebrate.
climb to the top of Carmel and pray alone, face to the ground.
games.why: he climbs to the top, puts his face between his knees and prays until a little cloud rises. that quiet waiting is what the hermits treasured.

practice: Find the quietest small spot within reach, the end of a sofa, a step outside, even a parked car, and sit low, leaning forward a little the way Elijah did. Don't ask for fire; just wait, the way his servant watched the sea.
If you pray, pray without words or with one line of a psalm; if not, rest in the quiet of your corner.

wordCard.voice: Carmelite. One who belongs to Carmel: the order that began with hermits on Elijah's mountain and gave its life to Mary. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Carmel, the name of the mountain in the books of Kings.

carryVoice: Your line: Elijah's mountain. Prayer can start as simply as going somewhere quiet and staying low. Until tomorrow.
